narrative:
The model estimates a 69% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest element pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have this same limited experience level, while many others bring 6 or more years; the system sees shorter tenure as a common pattern among those who eventually depart.

The second most influential factor is that you have received other job offers while working here. This strongly pushes the prediction toward leaving, as external opportunities often signal that someone is actively considering or being pulled elsewhere.

Third, your employment in the “other” sector also contributed to the decision to predict departure. This sector shows a noticeably lower retention rate in the data compared with fields like medical or education.

Taken together, these elements outweighed positive signals such as your high emotional commitment, recognition you receive, and overall job satisfaction.

The organization should consider discussing retention strategies with you, such as clearer promotion paths or expanded responsibilities that build on your experience. You may wish to reflect on whether the external opportunities align better with your long-term goals. Addressing these points openly could change the outlook for both sides. (248 words)
